instruments: HKMA guidance to Authorized Institutions on digital-asset custody and distribution
standing_summary: HKMA's core guidance to Authorized Institutions on digital-asset activity dates to 20 February 2024, issued as two same-day circulars -- one on custody of digital assets, the other on sale and distribution of tokenised products -- both requiring affected Authorized Institutions to notify HKMA and confirm they meet the expected standards within six months of the circular date. An April 2025 circular sets conduct and disclosure standards for Authorized Institutions providing staking services from custodial holdings (covering internal controls, fee/risk disclosure including slashing and hacking risk, and blockchain-protocol/third-party due diligence), conditional on discussing the arrangement with HKMA in advance; it sets standards for staking services rather than granting general permission to offer them. HKMA reissued updated custody guidance on 27 May 2026; secondary legal commentary describes this as expanding cyber-security, cold-wallet, and governance requirements, but that description is corroborated only by secondary sources -- the primary circular text could not be fetched during this research (HKMA's document repository, brdr.hkma.gov.hk, was unreachable) and should be verified directly before being relied on. On the retail digital-money side, HKMA completed Phase 2 of the e-HKD Pilot Programme on 28 October 2025 and stated that the immediate priority for e-HKD lies beyond retail use cases, redirecting near-term focus to wholesale payments and tokenisation-ecosystem support (branded e-HKD+). Tokenised deposits are being advanced operationally through Project Ensemble/EnsembleTX (see the Tokenization & RWA pillar) rather than through standalone tokenised-deposit guidance.

open_items: HKMA indicated further preparatory work toward a possible future retail e-HKD would continue into H1 2026; no published outcome of that work was found yet.
No standalone HKMA guidance on tokenised deposits exists yet; the topic is currently being handled through the Project Ensemble pilot rather than a codified circular.

The 27 May 2026 updated custody guidance circular is hosted on HKMA's banking-sector document repository (brdr.hkma.gov.hk), which was unreachable during this research (TLS certificate-chain failure to the live site; no Wayback Machine snapshot yet archived, likely due to the document's recency); its content above is corroborated only by secondary legal-commentary sources and should be re-confirmed directly against the primary text when the repository is reachable or an archived copy appears.

HKMA consulted (13 Jun 2025) on amendments -- described in the consultation's own title as a 'cryptoassets standard' plus other miscellaneous changes -- to banking return MA(BS)3 Part IIIc and its explanatory notes; the consultation's source page (brdr.hkma.gov.hk) returned a server error each time it was requested during this update, so the specific proposed changes, consultation deadline, and outcome are not yet confirmed against primary source text and should be checked directly once the page is reachable.

During a further update (26 Jul 2026), HKMA's domain was broadly unreachable: brdr.hkma.gov.hk returned HTTP 503 on every request, including for a 4 Sep 2025 HKAB letter on revised completion instructions for the Cryptoassets Standard and a 13 Jun 2025 consultation annex on MA(BS)3 Part II Cls completion instructions (both drafted as cards from title/metadata only, pending primary-text confirmation), and www.hkma.gov.hk returned no retrievable body text for at least one press/speech page tested that day. Since earlier updates did reach some brdr.hkma.gov.hk and www.hkma.gov.hk pages successfully (see other open_items and key_links above), this looks like a session-specific or intermittent access problem rather than a permanent one; it should be re-tried on the next pass and the affected cards' content re-confirmed against primary text once reachable.

A further check on 28 Jul 2026 found HKMA's entire web presence still unreachable -- brdr.hkma.gov.hk returned HTTP 503 on its document-ledger root and on every individual document URL tried (including the 13 Jun 2025 return-template consultation and the 11 Jul 2025 gazettal circular), and www.hkma.gov.hk returned no retrievable content for both a press-release page and two different PDFs (one a previously-cited stablecoin guideline, ruling out a problem specific to any one file). A control fetch of an unrelated regulator's site (SFC) succeeded at the same time, confirming this is an HKMA-specific problem, not a general fetch-tooling issue. Four more items from the same Cryptoassets Standard rollout -- two 13 Jun 2025 return-template annexes (MA(BS)3 Part IIIb; MA(BS)3a Part I), the original 23 Jul 2024 disclosure-requirements circular, and the 11 Jul 2025 gazettal-of-rules circular -- were drafted as cards from title/metadata only for the same reason, consistent with the two items noted above; all four, like those two, remain pending primary-text confirmation once HKMA's site is reachable again.

A further check on 29 Jul 2026 again found HKMA's web presence unreachable across multiple page types -- a www.hkma.gov.hk press-release page, a circular PDF, both the press-release and consultations RSS feeds, and brdr.hkma.gov.hk's document ledger all failed to return usable content -- while a control fetch of SFC's site succeeded at the same time, again pointing to an HKMA-specific problem rather than a general fetch-tooling issue. Two more items were drafted as cards from title/metadata only for the same reason: a 16 Apr 2024 circular setting out risk management considerations for Authorized Institutions' use of distributed ledger technology, and a consultation continuing the Cryptoasset Standard rollout on a revised SPM module CA-G-1 (the overview module of the capital adequacy regime for locally incorporated Authorized Institutions). That consultation is dated 23 Oct 2025 per its queue publish timestamp, though its own doc-ledger URL is dated one day earlier (22 Oct 2025); this discrepancy, its response deadline, and both items' substantive content all remain pending primary-text confirmation once HKMA's site is reachable again.
